text: Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this fixture in the Premier League, as Luton Town host Tottenham at Kenilworth Road.
Coming off the back of a first-ever Premier League victory, the Hatters were defeated 2-1 last time out by fellow promoted side Burnley.
Rob Edwards’ side secured that maiden win away at Everton, and will be hoping they notch another in front of their home fans sooner than later.
However, they face a Spurs side who are unbeaten in the league so far this season.

Recording five wins and two draws so far in 2022-23, Ange Postecoglou’s men sit second in the table, just a point behind Manchester City after securing a controversial 2-1 win over Liverpool in their last game.
Luton make three changes from their 2-1 loss to Burnley last time out, with three defenders taken out of the side.

With Amari’i Bell injured and Teden Mengi and Issa Kabore benched, Reece Burke and Mads Andersen come into the back three, while Jacob Brown pushes out to the right flank, allowing Elijah Adebayo to join the attack.
Spurs, meanwhile, make no changes to the side that beat Liverpool in the dying minutes, with opening goalscorer Son Heung-Min leading from the front.
Behind him, the attacking trifecta of Richarlison, James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski should cause Luton plenty of problems.
The two sides trudge out of the Kenilworth Road tunnel, and we're almost ready for kick-off in the first game of this Premier League weekend!
Son gets the match underway for Spurs, and we're off and running in Bedfordshire!

This is the first meeting between Luton and Tottenham in any competition since a goalless draw in the old First Division back in March 1992, the season in which the Hatters were relegated to miss out on the launch of the Premier League.
WIDE!!! Spurs blow the chance to go 1-0 up inside three minutes! Kulusevski cuts inside and whips a cross into the middle.
The bounce deceives Kaminski, but Richarlison closing in at the far post can only strike a half-volley wide.
That looked easier to score than miss for the Brazilian!

SAVED!!! Maddison turns on the edge of the box to feed Richarlison running in behind the Luton defence, but his low, side-footed shot is parried by the outstretched leg of Kaminski! It's been one-way traffic so far!
Porro races down the right edge before playing a pass inside to Son.
He shoots from the edge of the box, but Mpanzu is in the way of it for Luton.
WIDE!!! Son and Porro play successive one-two's to give the full-back a clear run into the box.
He engages Kaminski as he darts in behind, but skews a poor effort wide of the post with the goalkeeper beaten!
Morris comes forward on the break for Luton, and holds up the ball as the support arrives.
He cuts it back for Adebayo in the middle, but Romero steps in to cut the pass out and come away with possession!
OVER!!!! Porro's long cross-field pass is nodded down by Maddison, and the recipient Son smashes a half-volley which whistles over the top!
Spurs are unbeaten in nine league games against Luton, winning five since a 2-0 away defeat in November 1987; with Ian Allinson scoring a brace for the Hatters that day.

Richarlison and Udogie exchange passes down the near touchline as the Brazilian looks to run in behind, but he's shunted over by Brown off the ball, and wins a free-kick in a promising position for Tottenham.
Tottenham have won 12 of their last 14 Premier League games against promoted sides, and have already beaten Burnley and Sheffield United this season.
They've not lost to a side in their debut season in the competition since a 3-1 defeat by Blackpool in 2010-11.
Van de Ven comes forward and has space to shoot from 30 yards.
He does so, but the jeers from the crowd begin almost immediately afterwards as the ball sails into the stands.
SAVED!!! Kulusevski's whipped-in low cross towards Maddison is scythed away by a sliding Lockyer, but the ball drops kindly for Son in the box.
He shoots, but it's straight at Kaminski and the Hatters 'keeper makes a comfortable save!
Lockyer steps in to cut out another Spurs attack, but Richarlison picks up the scraps and curls a shot high and wide from the edge of the box.
Lockyer slides in to dispossess Maddison but gets nowhere near the ball as he takes the Spurs playmaker down on the edge of the box, and receives the first booking of the game.
Porro is dispossessed by Morris, who feeds Mpanzu running wide to his right.
His low cross towards Adebayo is half-cleared by Spurs, but Nakamba's follow-up shot is not-so-marvellous and skews well wide.
Brown pops up on the left flank and fires a cross towards the near post, which flies into the side-netting for a goal-kick despite the hosts demanding a corner!
Ogbene bursts past Porro to race into the left side of the Spurs box, but his cut-back for Mpanzu on the edge is thwarted by Sarr!
Luton win their first corner of the game following a Romero deflection behind, but Morris' front-post header is wayward and loops over the top.
Tottenham have won six of and are unbeaten in their last eight Premier League games, with no side currently on a longer run without defeat.
SAVED!!! Sarr latches onto a loose ball and drives through the middle into the final third.
He spreads it wide to Kulusevski, whose first-time shot across the face of goal is tipped wide by Kaminski at full stretch!
Ogbene does well to bring down and lay off Nakamba's aerial ball into the box, but Doughty's floated cross back in is easily caught by Vicario!
Maddison twists and turns away from Nakamba, but has his shirt dragged back by the Zimbabwean to win Spurs a free-kick which is well within their number 10's shooting range.
Maddison steps up to take the free-kick he won for Spurs, but his curling effort is whipped up and over the top of Kaminski's goal!
The two number nines come together as Morris accidentally clips Richarlison in the air, and the Luton striker is shown a yellow card for the challenge.
Luton have won just one of their last 10 home league games against London sides, beating Championship side QPR 3-1 in October last season.
Spurs pile numbers forward as they look to open Luton up, but neither Udogie, Richarlison or Porro can get a cross or shot away into the Hatters' packed box.
Ogbene does well to dispossess Porro, but doesn't get very far before being clipped late by Bissouma.
He's shown a yellow card, and having picked up five bookings in just eight games this season, the Spurs midfielder will receive a one-match suspension!
BALL IN THE NET!!! Doughty's free-kick is headed across goal by Morris, and Adebayo flicks the ball towards goal.

It flies up into the air and bounces back off the post, where Lockyer nods it in to potentially put Luton ahead! However, Adebayo had pushed Romero in order to reach the initial ball, and so it's a Spurs free-kick rather than a Luton goal!
Both Lockyer and Morris picked up knocks to the head during that sequence of play, and as they're assessed on the touchline, Luton are down to just nine players for the moment!
Tottenham have had more shots than any other Premier League side this season (138), with their average of 19.7 shots per game their highest on record in a single campaign.

They've had at least 20 efforts in three of their last four league games, as many times as they had done in their previous 28, and so far at Kenilworth Road, Spurs have managed to fire off 11 already!
Andersen concedes a corner as he steps in to cut out a Richarlison chance, but Maddison's delivery from the set-piece is headed clear at the front post by Burke!
We're into three additional minutes at Kenilworth Road as Spurs continue to chase that all-important opening goal!
CHANCE!!! Richarlison's low cross into the box is collected by Son, who then tees up Maddison from the edge of the box.
The England playmaker has time to pick his spot, but blazes a curling effort wide of the mark!
HE'S OFF!!! Bissouma drives through the middle before going down under pressure on the edge of the box.

It wasn't enough pressure though, says the referee, who shows the midfielder a second yellow card for simulation and then produces the red! After a first-half they've dominated, Spurs will now have to play out the rest of the game a player down!
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-0 TOTTENHAM.

It's all square at the break, with the hosts holding on despite a plethora of Tottenham chances! Kaminski has made saves from Richarlison, Son and Kulusevski, with the former, Porro and Maddison also firing wide as Spurs laid siege to the Luton box at times! The Hatters haven't been without chances of their own though, and saw a scrappy Lockyer goal disallowed thanks to a foul on Romero.

Luton will have renewed confidence going in to the second half too, not only having kept Spurs at bay so far, but also facing a side down to 10 men after Bissouma received a second yellow card late in the first.

12 shots to three having generated 1.72 xG shows just how freely Spurs have attacked in the first half, but with a zero in the goal column, and without Bissouma for the second half, Ange Postecoglou's side need to find a breakthrough and put this game to bed sharpish.
With Spurs needing a re-shuffle following Bissouma's sending off, and Richarlison is sacrificed for Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg to come on to and bolster the midfield.
Adebayo resumes proceedings at Kenilworth Road, and we're back underway hoping the first goal isn't too far away!
Kulusevski turns and bursts away from Nakamba to feed Son on the counter, but Burke steps in with a well-timed interception to cut out the Spurs captain's pass for Maddison in the box.
WIDE!!! What a chance for the Hatters! Ogbene gets rid of Udogie before crossing low towards the far post.
An unmarked Adebayo closes in with Vicario scrambling, but he puts the effort wide with the goal at his mercy!
Luton have now failed to score a first-half goal in seven of their eight games this season, more often than any other Premier League team.
Maddison drills a Spurs corner into the middle, but it's nodded away by Luton.
Hojbjerg follows in with a half-volley from the edge of the box, but Burke's block sends the ball behind for another corner.
GOOOOOOAAAALLL!!! Spurs finally make the breakthrough!!! Taking a short corner from the opposite side, Kulusevski and Maddison play a one-two which catches Luton off-guard.

The latter cuts the ball back towards Van de Ven, whose first-time shot beats Kaminski and nestles in the back of the net!! After a plethora of chances, the 10-man visitors lead 1-0 at Kenilworth Road!
Maddison's movement there was too much for Luton to handle, and he managed to squeeze the ball into Van de Ven's path for the centre-back to drill the opener home.
A loose Nakamba touch sees him stretching to reach the ball, and he's very lucky to avoid a card after catching Porro very late in the 50-50.
WIDE!!! Mpanzu floats a cross to the back post where Doughty is closing in, but the wing-back's left footed volley flashes across the face of goal and behind with Vicario beaten!

Maddison has now been directly involved in 22 goals across his last 23 away Premier League appearances, either scoring (three) or assisting (seven) in seven of his last eight on the road and managing another seven contributions in his last five games.
Fulcrum.
There's a break in play following an injury to Andersen, who is eventually replaced in the Hatters' defence by Teden Mengi.
SAVED!!! Luton win possession in the final third and Adebayo tees up Morris to his left.
The striker shoots from a tight angle, and the ball stings Vicario's fingertips as the goalkeeper makes the near-post save!
WIDE!!! Udogie drifts in-field and links up with Sarr, who passes right to Porro.
The right-back shoots from the edge of the box with the outside of his boot, and sends a curling shot inches wide of the post!
OVER!!! Doughty whips in a cross from the left with Brown the target, but the forward's effort is sent over the top despite having a free header!
After a Luton penalty shout comes to nothing, the Hatters make a triple substitution.
Brown is first off, and will be replaced by Luke Berry in midfield.
Adebayo also comes off following a determined if profligate performance up front, and Cauley Woodrow is on for the final 23 minutes.
Mpanzu is the third player taken off, and Tahith Chong enters the fray in place of Luton's longest-serving player.
SAVED!!! A poor header from Van de Ven allows Morris to flick the ball into Woodrow's path, but the striker scuffs his shot after running in behind and Vicario makes the save!
Ogbene glides past Hojbjerg with the ball, but is stopped soon afterwards by the Spurs midfielder's late challenge, which results in a yellow card for the Dane.

Following Van de Ven's opener, Tottenham have now had 167 different players score for them in the Premier League (excluding own goals), more than any other side in the competition's history (Newcastle & West Ham United each have 166).
Successive Luton corners are won on the right-hand side by Woodrow, but both crosses from Doughty don't reach Morris as Spurs head each one clear.
BLOCKED!!! Luton keep the ball alive from their latest corner and Doughty cuts inside from the right, but his curling shot takes a nick off Porro and flashes behind for another corner!
Ange Postecoglou is keen to protect his side's slender lead, and brings Emerson Royal onto the field in place of his captain Son.
Maddison also comes off as Spurs' objective becomes a defensive one, with Oliver Skipp on in the midfielder's place.

Tottenham have scored at least twice in all seven of their Premier League games under Ange Postecoglou – no manager has ever seen his team score 2+ goals in his first eight games in charge in the competition before.
Ogbene's cross drops for Doughty, who is forced wide but still manages to get a shot away, and the ball is deflected behind off Romero to give Luton yet another corner!
Luton captain Lockyer is taken off, and the introduction of an attack-minded midfielder in the form of Ross Barkley shows just how much the Hatters want to turn this game around.
Udogie is off in Spurs' latest alteration, and it's a direct replacement at left-back as Ben Davies enters the fray.
Spurs are unbeaten in eight matches under Ange Postecoglou this season, though one of their three draws saw them eliminated from the League Cup on penalties.
It's the best unbeaten start any Tottenham manager has had in the club's history, and it could be extended if they manage to hold on here!

There's less than five minutes of normal time left for Spurs to maintain their slender lead, but having made a raft of defensive substitutions, could that come back to bite them if Luton do manage to find an equaliser here?
In the second half, Luton have had eight efforts on goal to Spurs' three, showing the turnaround in attacking narrative since half-time.
However, despite six of these coming from inside the box, they've generated just 0.69 xG, and at the other end, Spurs have scored with one of their three attempts!
FIVE added minutes to play at Kenilworth Road, and with just one goal in it, there could still be plenty of twists and turns to come!
Kulusevski has been up front alone for the last few minutes, and is replaced late on for Alejo Veliz to do that job for Spurs in the dying minutes.
Porro has stayed down following an aerial clash with Chong, but play carries on until a free-kick is blown against Barkley for a foul on Emerson.

CHANCE!! Sarr races forward on the break and beats both Nakamba and Burke before finding Veliz in the box, but the substitute loses his footing as he goes to shoot and the chance is snuffed out by Luton!
Hojbjerg has trudged off injured for Spurs, leaving his side down to nine for the final 30 seconds of this contest!
Luton look to exploit Spurs' reshuffled defence and Mengi knocks it forward for Ogbene, but Vicario races out of his box to thump the ball clear!
Morris' last-gasp ball into the box is blocked and doesn't quite sit up for Chong, and the follow-up from Mengi flashes over the top as the full-time whistle goes!
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-1 TOTTENHAM.

It's all over at Kenilworth Road, as Spurs seal the three points in a backs-to-the-wall second half! After dominating the first half to no avail, the visitors finally broke through eight minutes into the second, with Van de Ven's well-taken strike putting his side 1-0 up.
From there though, it was all Luton, who peppered the Spurs goal through chances for Adebayo, Doughty, Brown, Morris and Woodrow.

Vicario made saves from the latter two as Spurs clung on to their slender lead, and despite having chances of their own through Porro and Veliz late on, it would remain a one-goal game which ended in Tottenham's favour.
A sixth victory in eight sees Ange Postecoglou's Spurs side climb to first in the table, maintaining their best start to a Premier League season.

Luton remain above the bottom three (for now) on goal difference, but having produced a fantastic, yet fruitless second-half performance against one of the division's best sides, it won't be long until that first home win is secured.
That's all from us, we hope you enjoyed the game! Until the next one comes around, it's goodbye for now.
